stories.headline: Stocks bounce back after their worst day since April 2025 as October jobs beat forecasts
stories.summary: US stocks rose on Friday after Thursday's selloff, which was the S&P 500's worst day since the April 2025 tariff crash and wiped out about $3 trillion in value. Employers added 165,000 jobs in October, more than expected, and unemployment fell to 4.1%. Short-term Treasury yields rose after the report, and the Dow stayed close to flat while the Nasdaq led the gains.

stories.headline: Chip stocks win back part of Thursday's record-scale rout
stories.summary: Nvidia, AMD and Micron led semiconductors higher on Friday, a day after the sector's worst selloff since 2020 on fears that a Democratic Congress would slow the AI data-center buildout. By mid-morning the big chip stocks had won back only about a third of Thursday's losses, and part of the early bounce faded.

stories.headline: Axon plunges after missing Q3 estimates and cutting its 2026 revenue outlook on drone delays
stories.summary: Axon missed third-quarter profit estimates and lowered its 2026 revenue forecast, blaming delays in federal drone deployments. It also said it would invest another $1.2 billion in drone maker Skydio. The stock fell almost 10% on Thursday, dropped as much as 25% after hours and kept falling on Friday, trading close to its 52-week low.

stories.headline: Microchip Technology sinks nearly 14% on a weak December-quarter forecast
stories.summary: Microchip guided December-quarter revenue to $1.61 billion at the midpoint, below the $1.63 billion consensus, because supply limits at foundries and assembly partners are delaying high-margin shipments. It was the worst performer in the Russell 1000 on Friday, falling 13.7% the day after the chip-sector crash.

stories.headline: Stocks plunge as Democratic midterm sweep stirs fears of AI regulation; Nasdaq enters correction
stories.summary: US stocks had their worst day in months on Nov. 5. The S&P 500 fell about 4.4%, the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.5% into correction territory, and the Dow lost 1,833 points. Investors sold AI and tech shares on worries that Democrats, after winning both chambers of Congress, will slow the data-center buildout. That reversed the previous day's post-election rally. Falling stocks outnumbered rising ones by about 6 to 1 on the NYSE, and small caps fell about as much as the large-cap indexes.

stories.headline: Chip stocks post their second-biggest drop on record, Nvidia turns negative for the year
stories.summary: The Philadelphia semiconductor index fell about 12%, its second-biggest one-day drop on record, as the post-election sell-off in AI hardware grew. Nvidia fell more than 9% and is now down for the year. The 'Magnificent Seven' together lost over $1 trillion in market value. Chips had already fallen sharply on Oct. 30 and over the days that followed, so the semis ETF is down about 20% in a week.

stories.headline: Data-center and AI infrastructure high-flyers tumble on fears of policy limits on the buildout
stories.summary: Data-center operators such as IREN, Applied Digital and Nebius fell steeply as investors weighed the risk that new Democratic majorities will restrict data-center construction. In Texas, a Democrat who campaigned on a statewide pause on data centers unseated Gov. Greg Abbott. Many of these stocks had multiplied in value over the past few years.

stories.headline: Crude oil drops more than 7% twice in three sessions as US-Iran war risk is repriced around the midterms
stories.summary: Brent fell 7.6% on Nov. 2 and 8.6% on Nov. 4, and WTI fell by similar amounts, before bouncing on Nov. 5. The US-Israeli war with Iran is still unresolved. Before the election President Trump threatened to renew strikes, but afterward he said he had no immediate plans to do so. On Nov. 5 Iran's Revolutionary Guard reported tankers on fire in the Strait of Hormuz. The sources found did not directly explain the Nov. 2 and Nov. 4 drops.
